title: Xuanwu Urgent Summoning
next_chapter_hook: As Mo Xiansheng's figure dissolved into the fragment, the chessboard fragment in Chen Ji's hand suddenly scorched hot—and seven blood-red characters appeared: 'Chapter Seven Hundred, Lethal Trap Opens.'

text.content: The moment Chen Ji stepped into the Xuanwu Sect Mountain Gate, he sensed something amiss. The disciples who usually came and go in a steady stream were nowhere to be seen; only a few walked hastily with their heads down, their faces filled with fear. An inexplicable oppression hung in the air, like the stillness before a storm. He stopped, his gaze sweeping across the massive stone in the plaza's center carved with the characters 'Xuanwu'—the cracks were now a third deeper than half a month ago.

dialogue.content: It seems quite a lot has happened in the sect during my absence.

text.content: He murmured to himself, his tone revealing no emotion. Only the fragment hidden in his sleeve felt faintly warm, as if warning him of something. Chen Ji continued forward composedly, his mind already racing through potential scenarios. Beneath his facade of a 'useless servant', his calculating heart never rested. He silently assessed every disciple passing by—who was a pawn, who was an opponent, and who... had already been bought.

dialogue.content: You've finally returned. I've been waiting for you for a long time.

text.content: The ancient voice didn't come from any particular direction but resounded directly in Chen Ji's Mental Sea. His footsteps faltered as he raised his head toward the main peak—Mo Xiansheng's presence was even more frail than before, yet there was an inexplicable...urgency about him. Chen Ji narrowed his eyes, his fingers subtly stroking the Tianji Record Fragment in his sleeve.

dialogue.content: Since my master summons, how dare I refuse. However... how long is this 'long time'? Three days ago, or three years?

text.content: He made no attempt to hide his suspicion. Three days ago, he was still dealing with Xuanwu Sect people a thousand miles away. If Mo Xiansheng truly possessed Heavenly Secrets foresight, why didn't he give advance warning? Unless... there was something he hadn't yet understood. A low laugh echoed in his Mental Sea, tinged with bitterness.

dialogue.content: Those who possess the Tianji Record cannot directly communicate with each other. I only know you would return today, but not what happened on your journey. This is the first thing I must tell you—regarding the Tianji Record, everything you think you know is merely the tip of the iceberg.

text.content: Chen Ji entered the hidden stone chamber behind the main peak. He'd been here several times before, but never had he felt such suffocating pressure. Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul phantom floated in mid-air, even more translucent than in memory, nearly transparent. Yet the light in those eyes was sharper than ever.

choice.prompt: Mo Xiansheng was about to reveal the secrets of the Tianji Record. How should Chen Ji respond to this conversation?

choices.description: Directly question Mo Xiansheng's true identity, disrupt his rhythm, seize conversational initiative
choices.visible_reward: Force Mo Xiansheng to reveal his hand prematurely
choices.risk_hint: May provoke the master's anger, losing the opportunity to gain information

text.content: Chen Ji offered no bow, speaking directly: 'Master, you call yourself my master, but when has the Tianji Record's inheritance ever distinguished between master and disciple? Who exactly are you?' The words fell, and the air in the stone chamber seemed to freeze.

choices.text: Retreat to advance, calmly observe the situation
choices.description: Maintain a respectful posture, let Mo Xiansheng reveal his cards first, then adjust strategy accordingly
choices.visible_cost: May fall into a passive position
choices.risk_hint: If Mo Xiansheng has ulterior motives, may miss the first opportunity

text.content: Chen Ji bowed his head: 'Your disciple is foolish, I humbly ask the master for guidance.' This humble posture caused Mo Xiansheng's phantom to flicker slightly, as if measuring his depths.

choices.text: Point directly to the core, question the purpose
choices.description: Directly confront Mo Xiansheng, demanding to know why he chose Chen Ji, shattering all pretentious pleasantries
choices.visible_reward: Obtain the truth at the fastest possible speed
choices.risk_hint: Possibly touching Mo Xiansheng's forbidden reverse scale

text.content: Chen Ji raised his head, his gaze sharp as a blade: "The disciple only wants to know one thing—did you choose me for the inheritance, or for... exploitation?"

Silence filled the stone chamber for a moment. Mo Xiansheng's phantom drifted closer, those deep eyes seeming to reflect the birth and death of countless stars. When he spoke again, his voice carried a desolation Chen Ji had never heard. "Good, very good. You possess more courage than my previous self." He paused, then continued, "Since you ask, this old man will no longer conceal—three hundred years ago, I too was a holder of the Tianji Record."

dialogue.content: The Tianji Record was far more complete back then, but the price was even more brutal. Every glimpse of the future drained the holder's lifespan and fortune. I spent fifty years sealing the Tianji Record within its fragments, and I myself became a remnant soul that could only依附于器物.

text.content: Chen Ji's pupils slightly contracted. Fifty years of foresight... That meant Mo Xiansheng had lived at least one hundred and fifty years, far surpassing an ordinary cultivator's lifespan. His expression remained unchanged, but his heart was already churning with waves. So the Tianji Record's curse was this terrifying—even former holders could not bear it.

Mo Xiansheng seemed to see through his thoughts, smiling bitterly: "Are you afraid? No need to hide it. When I learned the truth back then, I was even more terrified than you. But fate is cruel. When I tried to pass the fragment to someone else, the Tianji Record chose its next holder on its own—the child named Chen Xuan from Tianqing Sect." His voice trembled slightly, "And he... passed the inheritance to you twenty years ago."

dialogue.content: (Cold smile) So Master has been monitoring the disciple? Since your supposed "death"?

text.content: Chen Ji's voice carried a hint of mockery. What he despised most was being used as a chess piece, especially under the guise of "protection" while actually "spying." Mo Xiansheng was not angered; instead, he nodded: "Monitoring? No, I was merely waiting. Waiting for a turning point that could break this deadlock." As he spoke, he took out a black object from the void—a fragment the size of a palm, its surface covered with dense patterns, faintly emanating a chilling aura.

dialogue.content: This is a fragment of the chessboard I brought when I left the Tianji Pavilion. It can temporarily shield you from the surveillance of the Tianji Pavilion and the Holy Sect, giving you a period of true "invisibility." But it only has three uses remaining—once used up, it becomes worthless.

choice.prompt: Facing this precious strategic artifact, how should Chen Ji choose?

choices.description: Accept the fragment, promise to repay Mo Xiansheng if opportunities arise, establish a limited cooperative relationship
choices.visible_reward: Obtain a key item, gain strategic initiative
choices.risk_hint: May be further manipulated by Mo Xiansheng using this as leverage

text.content: Chen Ji remained silent for a moment, then reached out to take the chessboard fragment. The moment it touched his palm, a cool sensation seeped into his heart, as if some invisible shackles were temporarily loosened. He did not thank Mo Xiansheng, simply placing the fragment into his sleeve beside the Tianji Record Fragment. "This favor, the disciple will remember."

choices.text: Question the motives, demand equal exchange
choices.description: Not take things for nothing, require Mo Xiansheng to first reveal his true purpose before deciding whether to cooperate
choices.visible_reward: Force out all of Mo Xiansheng's hidden cards
choices.risk_hint: If Mo Xiansheng turns hostile, may lose the only opportunity to obtain information

text.content: Chen Ji did not reach out his hand, merely gazing quietly at the fragment. "Master, you've hidden this treasure for three hundred years, and now you hand it to the disciple so easily—there should be an explanation, right?" His tone was calm, yet carried an undeniable force. Mo Xiansheng was stunned for a moment, then burst into hearty laughter. "Good, good! I果然没看错你！"

choices.text: Refuse the fragment, demonstrating an independent stance
choices.description: Unwilling to owe anyone a favor, would rather continue living under the shadows of two major forces than lose absolute freedom
choices.visible_cost: Losing protection from an important item
choices.visible_reward: Proving to Mo Xiansheng that he is no one's pawn
choices.risk_hint: Future actions will face greater risks

text.content: Chen Ji stepped back, hands clasped in salute: "Your kindness, Master, I gratefully accept. But this fragment is too precious, your disciple... cannot accept it." Mo Xiansheng's gaze suddenly turned sharp, then quickly dimmed. "You child... even more stubborn than your master Chen Xuan."

Mo Xiansheng's laughter gradually ceased, his expression becoming unprecedentedly solemn. He floated deeper into the stone chamber, back turned to Chen Ji, his voice low as if echoing from ancient times. "You wish to know my true purpose? Very well, I shall tell you—I despise the Heavenly Secrets Pavilion." He spun around sharply, the burning radiance of his remnant soul illuminating the entire chamber. "Three hundred years ago, they chose me, forced the Tianji Record upon me, yet abandoned me like refuse when I could no longer bear its weight."

dialogue.content: Cultivating you is to demonstrate to the Heavenly Secrets Pavilion—that the 'discarded piece' they released can nurture someone capable of shattering the heavenly chess game. I will reduce their ten-thousand-year scheme to ashes!

text.content: Chen Ji listened in silence, his expression utterly unmoved. He had witnessed countless noble justifications, each merely wrapping selfish desires in elaborate packaging. Mo Xiansheng's hatred was genuine, but that did not mean his goodwill toward Chen Ji was equally sincere. He spoke slowly, his voice terrifyingly calm: "Master speaks withcandid. Then your disciple must also ask—if the Heavenly Secrets Pavilion truly falls, how does Master intend to handle your disciple?"

dialogue.content: (Long silence)...I do not know. Perhaps you will break free from the Tianji Record's curse and attain true freedom; perhaps you will follow my footsteps and become the next remnant soul. But one thing I can be certain of—your fate has become intertwined with mine.

choice.prompt: Facing Mo Xiansheng's candor and the unknown, Chen Ji must make his final declaration

choices.text: Accept cooperation and break the deadlock together
choices.description: Since goals align, why not form a temporary alliance and each take what we need in the process of confronting the Heavenly Secrets Pavilion
choices.visible_cost: Risk of being implicated by Mo Xiansheng's personal vendetta in the future
choices.visible_reward: Gain Mo Xiansheng's complete knowledge and resource support
choices.risk_hint: Mo Xiansheng's judgment may not be correct, potentially leading Chen Ji into a deadly trap

text.content: Chen Ji extended his hand and accepted the chessboard fragment. This time, he did not hesitate. "Since Master wishes to oppose the Heavenly Secrets Pavilion, your disciple shall accompany you on this journey. But let me be clear—if one day Master treats your disciple as a discarded piece, I will never passively await my doom."

choices.text: Maintain distance and engage in limited cooperation
choices.description: Acknowledge Mo Xiansheng's hatred, but only willing to provide assistance under the premise of not affecting one's own safety
choices.visible_cost: Unable to obtain Mo Xiansheng's full support
choices.visible_reward: Free to advance or retreat, bound by no one
choices.risk_hint: Mo Xiansheng may consequently hold back

text.content: Chen Ji picked up the fragment, merely turning it in his palm. "Your disciple is willing to cooperate with Master against the Heavenly Secrets Pavilion, but only to this extent. Your disciple has their own path to walk and will not sacrifice themselves for anyone else's vendetta." Mo Xiansheng's eyes flickered, seemingly both disappointed and gratified by this answer.

choices.text: Reverse the scripting and seize the initiative
choices.description: Avoid making a clear statement, instead paint a grander vision for Mo Xiansheng, causing him to rely on oneself instead
choices.visible_cost: requires long-term maintenance of the deception
choices.visible_reward: completely draw Mo Xiansheng into his own chess game
choices.risk_hint: once exposed, he would utterly forfeit Mo Xiansheng's trust

text.content: Chen Ji tilted the corner of his lips, revealing a meaningful smile. "Master, you only think of dealing with the Tianji Pavilion, yet you know not that your disciple harbors far greater ambitions." He drew closer. "If your disciple could completely destroy the Heavenly Dao Chess Game, what do you think... would the Tianji Pavilion or the Holy Sect fall first?" Mo Xiansheng froze, then blazing fervor ignited in his eyes.

The atmosphere within the stone chamber shifted subtly. Mo Xiansheng gazed upon this young man as if seeing his three-hundred-year-old self—that spirited youth who dared to challenge the Heavenly Dao with his own strength. But he had ultimately fallen, defeated by fate, defeated by his own weakness. Now, placing his bet on thistrash disciple—was it hope he saw, or was he doomed to repeat his past mistakes?

dialogue.content: Your fate is even harder to read than mine. But remember, the true breaking point lies not in the past, but in that moment of Chapter Seven Hundred.

text.content: As the words fell, Mo Xiansheng's form began to dissolve, like a candle flame scattered by the wind. His voice grew ever more distant, yet each syllable seared distinctly into Chen Ji's Mental Sea: "The chessboard fragment... use it well... Chapter Seven Hundred... you and I... shall both be there that day..." The final thread of light vanished into the Void, leaving Chen Ji standing alone in the chamber's center, his hand clutching tightly the fragment that bore three centuries of accumulated power.

Chen Ji lowered his gaze to the chessboard fragment, a faint smile curling his lips. Chapter Seven Hundred? That meant he still had eighty-six chapters of time to scheme. Enough for him to accomplish much. He tucked the fragment alongside the Tianji Record Fragment into his sleeve, turning toward the chamber's exit. Beyond the door, sunlight shone bright, yet it could not reach the fathomless depths of his eyes.
